name: Void
label: Dischord
lede: Four kids from a planned suburb in Maryland, each playing as fast as he could and not always at the same time, and one side of a split LP that people are still trying to explain.

eras.title: Nothing to do in a model town
eras.text: Columbia, Maryland was one of the first planned communities in the country: tidy lawns, organized everything, thirty miles north of Washington. Dischord's own history calls it the perfect birthplace for a band as completely chaotic as Void.

q: Your lawn had to look a certain way.
years.h: Void, named for Black Sabbath's Into the Void
years.p: Four Columbia High School kids, [[John Weiffenbach|c415a399-2299-4899-b0d7-5fb1087e0c0f]], [[Bubba Dupree|faa35f26-bda4-4dd0-9d92-121e616d955a]], [[Chris Stover|e8c9149b-3ac0-4852-8425-3b9d6e8c0b53]] and [[Sean Finnegan|b5dac872-bd13-49df-b97f-f81c16f003ed]], start Void, taking the name from Black Sabbath's Into the Void.
years.xp: There wasn't much to do in Columbia besides sports and hanging around, as Bubba Dupree tells it, so any excuse to get to a show in D.C. or Baltimore was a good one. Chris Stover's road into the scene ran through Oddfellows Hall in Towson, where he saw [[The Teen Idles|84e8d8bf-da21-4488-89e5-50a4c12ff4fa]] and met [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] and [[Jeff Nelson|51f7994c-949d-4dbe-89eb-2c33f42a5620]].

years.h: Void's first show: the Wilson Center
years.p: Void debut at the Wilson Center in D.C., each member playing his own part as fast as he can, not necessarily together. Some hear noise; others hear something nobody else is doing.

eras.title: Two sessions in two months
eras.text: Void were barely out of their first year of shows when they cut thirty songs across two 1981 sessions. The Hit and Run session vanished for three decades. The Inner Ear session put them on Dischord's first compilation, Flex Your Head.

years.h: Void record ten songs at Inner Ear
years.p: In December 1981, a month after the Hit and Run session, Void cut ten songs at Inner Ear in Arlington. It gives up the Flex Your Head tracks and, a decade later, the Condensed Flesh seven-inch.

eras.title: Half an LP with Faith
eras.text: 1982 was Void's year on record. They made the Dischord sampler, played New York, and split an LP with Faith: two bands, two approaches to speed, one sleeve.

years.p: Void's Dehumanized, Authority and My Rules go on Dischord's compilation, next to [[Minor Threat|09037f07-42bc-46ac-a1ee-37f834451fee]], [[The Teen Idles|84e8d8bf-da21-4488-89e5-50a4c12ff4fa]] and [[SOA|e54cb250-3502-4c32-9482-70488bd9a8cb]].

years.h: Void tour the Northeast and play CBGB
years.p: Void start touring the Northeast, with a stop at CBGB in New York. A band that couldn't find anything to do in Columbia is now playing the Bowery.

Twelve Void songs, recorded with Don Zientara at Inner Ear in June 1982, on one side, [[Faith|f735a867-9a16-451f-8f83-669ed42e2574]] on the other. Critic Doug Mosurock later called Void's side quintessential American hardcore.
years.xp:
[[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] pitched pairing Void with Faith, and Void were happy to join the Dischord family. The two halves play like an argument: Faith are tight and furious, Void sound like four people falling down a staircase in formation.

The record outlived both bands: Dischord reissued it in 1985 and again in a remastered edition in 2008.

eras.title: The album nobody put out
eras.text: Void signed with Touch and Go and made a full album. Then the band ended, and the record stayed on the shelf, where bootleggers found it as Potions for Bad Dreams and a few future heavy bands learned from it.

years.h: Void's Touch and Go album stays in the can
years.p: Void sign with Touch and Go and record an album. By the time it could come out the band is gone, and label owner Corey Rusk isn't interested in releasing an album by a band that no longer exists.
years.xp:
Tapes of the Touch and Go session got around anyway, and bootleggers circulated it as Potions for Bad Dreams. According to Wikipedia, citing Chris Stover's interview with Vice, [[White Zombie|cfe572bf-840f-4bed-934a-f69f4b1e90d4]] and [[Melvins|9ccfbc94-a4f4-42f7-b6f5-d903ab77cccb]] have said it shaped their own sound.

Asked about it decades later, Stover said some things are better left unreleased. Bubba Dupree was blunter.

years.p: Dischord dates Void's end to fall 1984. Of the four members, only Bubba Dupree keeps making music.

eras.title: The legend grows without them
eras.text: With Void gone, the records did the work. Dischord reissued Faith/Void, and the small label Eye 95 finally gave the Inner Ear session its own seven-inch, Condensed Flesh.

years.p: Dischord reissues the 1982 Faith and Void split LP.
Songs from Void's December 1981 Inner Ear session finally get their own seven-inch, including Black, Jewish & Poor and War Hero.

eras.title: Emptying the vaults
eras.text: Void's afterlife picked up speed in the 2000s: the death of drummer Sean Finnegan, a Faith/Void remaster, and the Dischord archive release Sessions 1981-83, built around twenty songs nobody outside the band had heard.

years.p: Sean Finnegan dies of an apparent heart attack, Dischord reported. He had been working on the set of HBO's The Wire.
years.xp: Sean Finnegan drummed on every record Void made. His family held the viewing in Ellicott City, Maryland, not far from Columbia, and asked for donations to the Fisher House at Walter Reed in place of flowers.

years.p: Dischord releases a digitally remastered edition of the 1982 Faith and Void split LP.

years.h: Sessions 1981-83: Void's lost Hit and Run tapes · Dischord No. 171
years.p: Void's 20-song November 1981 Hit and Run session sat in a box for 30 years. Dischord released it in 2011 with the Inner Ear tapes, Faith/Void outtakes and two songs from a July 1983 show.
years.xp: Steve Carr recorded the Hit and Run session, and Bubba Dupree later admitted he didn't remember recording most of it. [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] mixed the collection, pressed on blue vinyl.

years.p: Void guitarist Bubba Dupree, who spent the 1990s and 2000s guesting with Soundgarden, Moby and [[Dave Grohl|4d5f891d-9bce-45ae-ad86-912dd27252fa]], joins 3rd Secret, the Seattle band built around former members of Nirvana and Soundgarden.
Eye 95 presses a 30th anniversary edition of Void's 1992 seven-inch on translucent gold-orange vinyl.
